I am an old woman here in Phalombe, and my small piece of land must feed my family. The rains can be hard here in the south, and my plot is small, so I must be careful. If the coupon from FISP comes, I will put a little fertilizer on my maize, but not too much because the land is small and the bag is expensive. I keep some manure from my goats and chickens to mix in, and I plant my maize together with pigeon peas like we always do. I cannot afford pesticide or to hire people — my own hands and my children will do the work.
